technology_name: High-Performance Concrete Enhanced with Hybrid Fibres (HFRHPC)
institution: KSCSTE - National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC)
problem_solved: Sudden brittle structural failures, micro-crack progression, and poor long-term durability in traditional concrete exposed to heavy traffic loads.
description: A specialized concrete variant—Hybrid Fibre Reinforced High-Performance Concrete (HFRHPC)—engineered using an M35 grade baseline. The mix partially replaces standard cement with Ground Granulated Blast-Furnace Slag (GGBS) at 30%, 50%, and 70% ratios to densify the matrix. It introduces an optimized multi-scale hybrid reinforcement system combining micro-polypropylene and macro-polypropylene fibers that work across different dimensional scales to arrest crack formation.
applications:
• Long-lasting overlay systems (white-topping) for heavy-traffic highways and urban intersections

• High-strength precast panels, retaining structures, and prestressed civil elements

• Structural repair, high-durability retrofitting, and rehabilitation of aging infrastructure

• Specialty ready-mix concrete formulations for demanding architectural and marine environments
